findings.title: Gaza's makeshift sewage pits pose growing threat to health, environment and groundwater
findings.location: Gaza Strip; displacement sites including Gaza City, Al-Mawasi/Khan Younis, central and northern Gaza
findings.affected_population_system: Displaced families; sewage treatment and pumping capacity; groundwater and water access; residents exposed to unlined cesspits
findings.summary: Newly recovered WAFA feature attributes to the Palestinian Water Authority a Gaza-wide estimate of 55,000 m³/day of untreated wastewater (about 40,000 into the sea, 15,000 through pits/leaks into the surrounding environment), five main treatment plants not operating, only 18 of 74 wastewater pumping stations partly functional and over 320,000 soakaway pits. Displaced residents also describe sewage pooling, contaminated water and health/safety hazards. These are newly surfaced quantified operating-capacity details, not proof that the deterioration happened in this hour; the agency does not give the authority figures' original measurement date.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: The authority said all five main wastewater treatment plants had ceased operating, while only 18 of the Strip's 74 pumping stations were functioning partially.
findings.source_verification: WAFA article accessed directly and dated 22 Nov 2026, 13:39 Gaza-local; the underlying Water Authority report/date and individual statistics were not independently corroborated.

bounded_discovery_context.prior_heartbeat_comparison: The 03:45 PST previous WAFA index inspection had latest Gaza news at 11:42 Gaza-local; the 13:39 feature was not then present in the captured index. The prior run already covered a separate meningitis/water-sanitation warning, but did not document the newly recovered quantitative pumping/cesspit capacity.

bounded_discovery_context.duplicate_handling: No new casualties counted; meningitis warning treated as already known rather than an independent new finding.
